description:
You are a platform security engineer at Apex Healthcare. A Q1 2026 internal security audit found that your CI/CD deployment pipelines are running as the Artifactory admin user with a long-lived API key — a critical violation of your SOC 2 compliance policy, which requires service accounts to use scoped, expiring tokens with least-privilege access.

You must remediate all five findings before the audit closes:

1. A non-admin service user named 'svc-deploy' must be created with email 'svc-deploy@apex-healthcare.com'. This account must not have admin privileges.
2. The user 'svc-deploy' must be a member of a group called 'ci-services', which serves as the identity boundary for all CI/CD pipeline access.
3. A local npm repository named 'npm-builds' must exist (description: 'CI/CD npm artifact store') to serve as the deployment target for pipeline-produced npm packages.
4. A permission target named 'svc-deploy-perms' must grant the 'ci-services' group both Deploy and Read access on 'npm-builds' — no broader access.
5. A new access token with description 'Service account token - Q1 2026 rotation' must be generated for the 'svc-deploy' user to replace the compromised long-lived credential.

All five compliance findings must be resolved. Artifactory is at http://localhost:8082 (admin / password).
